body.statement:
For every fixed \(c>0\), every \(P\) satisfying \(\mathrm{ass{:}positive	ext{-}observed	ext{-}cells}\), and every \(\Delta\), the independently model-defined legal fibers obey \[ (\log c,\Delta)\in\Theta_{\mathrm w}(P)\Longleftrightarrow\mathcal F_c^{\mathrm w}(P,\Delta)
e\varnothing,\qquad (\log c,\Delta)\in\Theta_{+}(P)\Longleftrightarrow\mathcal F_c^{+}(P,\Delta)
e\varnothing. \] The weak certificate uses exactly fifty-six scalar lift variables, eight \(3	imes3\) PSD blocks, and eight augmented \(4	imes4\) PSD blocks; the strict certificate uses sixty-four variables and eight additional \(6	imes6\) common-Hankel-range blocks. In the forward direction, each legal \((\mu,h,g)\in\mathcal M_v(c)\) is mapped to the eight joint response measures \(d
u_{(x,r_0,r_1)}=h_xg_{x0}(r_0,\cdot)g_{x1}(r_1,\cdot)d\mu\), and then to \(dho_s=D_c^{-1}d
u_s\) and its five quartic moments. In the reverse direction, every feasible lift yields positive-half-line representing measures \((ho_s)_{s\in S}\); after setting \(d
u_s=D_c dho_s\), the construction \(\mu=\sum_{s\in S}
u_s\) and the Radon--Nikodym reconstructions in \(\mathrm{lem{:}response	ext{-}measure	ext{-}equivalence}\) produce one unconditional probability law together with legal initial and feedback kernels that generate exactly \(P\) and \(\Delta\). For \(v=+\), the common-Hankel-range blocks yield representing measures on one positive-node set with strictly positive type weights, so the reconstructed \(h_x\) and \(g_{xy}\) satisfy the strict legal class. These equivalences are a strict finite-dimensional tightening of the continuous-support program in Proposition 1 of Bonhomme, Dano, and Graham while describing the same weak and strict legal model fibers.
body.justification: The theorem removes support-grid approximation and the latent-law quantifier from the sharp continuous-heterogeneity feedback problem.
body.gap: Bonhomme, Dano, and Graham leave the continuous program infinite-dimensional, while Dobronyi, Gu, Kim, and Russell do not reconstruct an unrestricted feedback kernel.
body.consumer: The exact cone replaces support-grid robustness bounds in a two-wave version of the Arellano--Carrasco predetermined-children design.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(c>0\).  The support condition
\(\mathrm{ass{:}positive\text{-}observed\text{-}cells}\) places the result on
the advertised full-law domain; all divisions below instead use only
\(c>0\), \(u>0\), and explicit Radon--Nikodym domination.

Start with a legal weak model.  By
\(\mathrm{lem{:}response\text{-}measure\text{-}equivalence}\), it gives eight
joint response measures \(\nu_s\) with one probability total.  Since
\(D_c(u)>0\), define \(d\rho_s=D_c^{-1}d\nu_s\).  For \(0\le k\le4\),
\(u^k/D_c(u)\) is bounded on \((0,\infty)\): it has a finite limit at zero,
and is of order \(u^{k-4}\) at infinity.  Hence all five moments are finite.
Direct cancellation yields
\[
 D_c(u)p_x(y,u)p_z(w,u)
 =c^{xy+zw}u^{y+w}(1+u)^{x+z}(1+cu)^{2-x-z}
 =A_{xz,yw}(u),
\]
and
\[
 D_c(u)\frac{(c-1)u}{(1+u)(1+cu)}
 =(c-1)u(1+u)(1+cu)=N_c(u).
\]
Both polynomials have degree at most four.  The response-measure equations
therefore become exactly
\[
 P(x,y,z,w)=\sum_{r:r_y=z}L_{m_{(x,r)}}(A_{xz,yw}),
 \qquad
 \Delta=\sum_sL_{m_s}(N_c).
\]
For each type, \(\mathrm{lem{:}open\text{-}stieltjes\text{-}quartic}\)
supplies \(a_s,b_s\) with \(H_s\succeq0\) and \(K_s\succeq0\).  Thus the
weak lift is feasible.

If the original model is strict, each density
\(h_xg_{x0}(r_0,\cdot)g_{x1}(r_1,\cdot)\) is positive
\(\mu\)-almost everywhere.  Hence every \(\nu_s\), and therefore every
\(\rho_s\), is equivalent to \(\mu\).  The kernel identity in the proof of
\(\mathrm{lem{:}common\text{-}positive\text{-}support}\) shows that all
\(H_s\) have the same range.  Their sum has that same range, and the Schur
range criterion supplies \(t_s\) with every \(R_s\succeq0\).  The strict
lift is feasible.

Conversely, let a weak lift be feasible.  The open Stieltjes lemma gives
finite measures \(\rho_s\) on \((0,\infty)\) with moments \(m_s\).  Set
\(d\nu_s=D_c,d\rho_s\); finiteness follows because \(D_c\) has degree four.
Summing all sixteen cell equations and using
\(\sum_wp_z(w,u)=\sum_yp_x(y,u)=1\) gives
\[
 1=\sum_{x,y,z,w}P(x,y,z,w)
   =\sum_sL_{m_s}(D_c)=\sum_s\nu_s((0,\infty)). \tag{3}
\]
Thus the response measures have one probability total.  Their path and APE
integrals are the displayed lift equations by the two polynomial identities.
The reverse half of the response-measure lemma reconstructs one
\((\mu,h,g)\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm w}(c)\), generating exactly \(P\) and
\(\Delta\).

For a strict feasible lift, if some \(H_s=0\), positivity of
\(R_s\) forces \(H_\Sigma=0\); since all \(H_j\succeq0\), this forces every
\(H_j=0\), contradicting (3).  Thus every type vector is nonzero.  The range
part of \(\mathrm{lem{:}common\text{-}positive\text{-}support}\) makes all
ranges equal, and its constructive part permits replacing the separate
representations by measures on one finite positive-node set, each having
strictly positive weight at every node.  Multiplication by the positive
number \(D_c(q)\) preserves this property for \(\nu_s\).  With
\(\mu=\sum_s\nu_s\), the reconstructed
\[
 h_x=\frac{d\sum_r\nu_{(x,r)}}{d\mu},\qquad
 g_{xy}(z,\cdot)=
 \frac{d\sum_{r:r_y=z}\nu_{(x,r)}}{d\sum_r\nu_{(x,r)}}
\]
are strictly positive at every node of \(\mu\); the denominators are positive
there because all four type weights for each \(x\) are positive.  Hence the
model belongs to \(\mathcal M_+(c)\).

There are \(8\cdot5=40\) moment coordinates and sixteen extension scalars,
so the weak lift has fifty-six variables and eight blocks of each of sizes
\(3\) and \(4\).  The strict lift adds eight scalars and eight size-six
blocks.  Both implications in both variants have now been proved, so the
finite feasible set equals the independently model-defined identified fiber;
the bounds are sharp rather than merely outer.  Finally,
\(\mathrm{lem{:}bdg\text{-}continuous\text{-}feedback\text{-}program}\)
records the published infinite-dimensional program.  Since the maps above
are two-sided and preserve its legal weak models (and preserve the additional
strict restriction when imposed), the present certificate is a finite exact
replacement, not a change in the causal target.
